steps.title: Mediterranean food
steps.body: Carignan's acidity and tannin suit hearty Mediterranean food: cassoulet, grilled lamb, sausages, stews with olives and herbs, and roast vegetables. Its earthy, herbal notes match rosemary, thyme and garlic. Old-vine examples suit game and aged cheeses.

steps.title: Service and age
steps.body: Serve at 16 to 18 degrees. Simple Carignan is best young. Old-vine wines from Priorat, Maule or the Languedoc can age 10 to 15 years, as acidity keeps them fresh. Decant young, firm examples.

steps.prompt: Which dish suits an old-vine Carignan?
steps.explanation: Hearty, fatty dishes balance its acidity and tannin.

steps.body: Carbonic maceration Carignan, light and juicy, is a good chilled red for summer barbecues.

steps.prompt: Carignan's high acidity helps old-vine examples age.
steps.explanation: Yes. Acidity preserves freshness over time.

steps.title: What you learned
points: Carignan suits cassoulet, lamb and herby stews
Serve at 16 to 18 degrees; decant young wines
